method.exclude_correction: Earlier recorded syncs used unanchored patterns ('data/', 'results/', 'tmp/'). In rsync an unanchored pattern matches a directory of that name at ANY depth, so nested directories such as vendor/academic-figure-generator/backend/data/ were silently skipped. This run anchors every pattern with a leading '/' and pushes the previously skipped nested files.
method.verification: sorted '<bytes>|<path>' manifest of every regular file on both sides, plus SHA-256 of the nine record files, plus a symlink target manifest

known_caveats: All 17 synced symlinks are dangling on the Linux remote because they encode macOS absolute targets (e.g. /Users/rocket/.../data/vae_official_ft_mse/... and /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.13/...). The record tree is byte-identical; only these links do not resolve. Rewriting them to relative paths would change preserved records and was not done.
Top-level data/ (~33 GB) and results/ (~28 GB) are deliberately local-only; the remote never held them. Nested data/ and results/ directories are now synced.
.venv/, .venv-cut3r/, tmp/ and tools/deepseek-harness/{runtime,state}/ are deliberately not synced.
The 1.5 GB CUDA SIF lives at the remote ~/gwm-images/ outside the project tree and must not be synced back.
Size|path manifest equality is a strong but not cryptographic check; the nine record files were additionally hash-verified.
open_items: Re-run this same anchored-exclude sync after any future long push, and check the transfer actually completed rather than assuming the background rsync finished.
Consider a recorded pre/post manifest hash in each future sync so interruption is detectable without a manual diff.
